findings.title: [P2] Apply source whitespace stripping to native creation candidates
findings.body: Native creationInfo candidates retain whitespace-only text unchanged. For example, <author> </author> produces candidate author=" ", whereas the pinned stylesheet's xsl:strip-space removes that text node and produces an empty author. Comparing the corresponding QML and native records therefore reports a revision conflict and suppresses content-matched recovery despite equivalent source-derived metadata. Preserve the original text in raw_creation, but account for source whitespace stripping in candidate fields, including applicable xml:space handling, or fail closed when equivalence cannot be established.

findings.title: [P2] Check colliding outside identities across the document root
findings.body: The outside-object scan starts at eventParameters, so it misses publicID-bearing objects elsewhere inside the document root. Adding a BED pick beside eventParameters with the same publicID as the selected pick leaves the representation ok and the pick uniquely accepted, despite the protocol requiring an outside same-type duplicate to make it unknown. The native scan has the same limitation at line 487. Inspect the whole root for colliding outside identities while retaining the existing projection scope.

findings.title: [P2] Validate use flags on all referenced-origin arrivals
findings.body: Arrivals from every referenced origin participate in pick selection, but projected_weight validates flags only for the preferred origin later in the function. A second referenced origin containing timeUsed="yes", or duplicate timeUsed children, therefore leaves the native representation ok even though these scoped fields violate the frozen fail-closed policy. This also allows that representation to lend its profile to QML. Validate flags and weight singletons for every referenced-origin arrival, while retaining only preferred-origin arrivals in the comparison output.

overall_explanation: The comment/PI boundary rejection implements the intended v2 policy, but source whitespace handling and two scoped-validation gaps violate the supplied contracts. Review used read-only inspection; no tests, transforms, or network requests were executed.
